findings.statement: CHI3L1 has one of the strongest and most reproducible increases of UC mucosa, significant upward in every one of the eight cohorts: pooled log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.87] with padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=5.78e-29].

CHI3L1 is already raised in non-inflamed mucosa of the discovery cohort [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.84] and rises further in inflamed versus non-inflamed mucosa of the same patients [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.62].

At protein level CHI3L1 is higher in inflamed UC mucosa in the same direction as the RNA change, although the proteomics authors did not call it significant and the protein change is much smaller than the RNA change: log2 ratio [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607], padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; padj=0.00013].

The CHI3L1 increase holds after adjustment for colon segment, age and sex: adjusted log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_adjusted; source=DATASET:GSE193677; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed UC vs control, biopsy level; adjusted_log2fc=3.732], padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_adjusted; source=DATASET:GSE193677; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed UC vs control, biopsy level; adjusted_padj=7.94e-42].

CXCL8 rises strongly across cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.86], padj [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=5.54e-29]) but is unchanged in non-inflamed mucosa [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.004] (padj [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=0.986]) and up in inflamed versus non-inflamed mucosa of the same patient [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.97]: a marker of local inflammation.

HMGCS2, the ketogenesis enzyme of colonocytes, is among the most consistently lost genes (pooled log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.84], padj [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=1.13e-21]), and the loss replicates at protein level: log2 ratio [gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094], padj [gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; padj=1.99e-13].

The HMGCS2 loss is local to inflamed mucosa: no change in non-inflamed mucosa [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.06] (padj [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=0.675]) and a paired inflamed versus non-inflamed loss [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-1.95]; it holds after covariate adjustment [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_adjusted; source=DATASET:GSE193677; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed UC vs control, biopsy level; adjusted_log2fc=-2.148].

AQP8, the colonocyte water channel, is the most strongly reduced gene (pooled log2FC [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.25], padj [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=5.79e-17]); it is slightly reduced already in non-inflamed mucosa [gene=AQP8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.50] and lower at protein level [gene=AQP8; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-1.396].

AQP8 does not reach significance in the small Leuven infliximab cohort despite a large fold change (padj [gene=AQP8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE16879; layer=rna; cohort=GSE16879; contrast=uc_vs_control; padj=0.169]), while the paediatric PROTECT rectum shows the largest loss [gene=AQP8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE109142; layer=rna; cohort=GSE109142; contrast=uc_vs_control; log2fc=-7.97].

The tight-junction claudin CLDN8 is lost in UC mucosa, significant in every cohort (pooled log2FC [gene=CLDN8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-4.29], padj [gene=CLDN8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=2.18e-23]).

The gluconeogenic enzyme PCK1 is consistently lost, part of the loss of colonocyte metabolism (pooled log2FC [gene=PCK1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.90], padj [gene=PCK1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=9.44e-22]).

UGT2A3, a colonocyte detoxification enzyme, is reduced (pooled log2FC [gene=UGT2A3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.52], padj [gene=UGT2A3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=5.74e-30]).

DUOXA2, the maturation factor of the epithelial NADPH oxidase DUOX2, has the largest pooled increase among genes measured in all cohorts (log2FC [gene=DUOXA2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.99], padj [gene=DUOXA2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=3.03e-18]).

DUOX2 rises in every cohort (pooled log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.41]) and the increase replicates at protein level: log2 ratio [gene=DUOX2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=1.468], padj [gene=DUOX2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; padj=1.07e-09].

S100A8, one chain of calprotectin, rises strongly (pooled log2FC [gene=S100A8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.77]) and is confirmed as protein: log2 ratio [gene=S100A8; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=2.749], padj [gene=S100A8; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; padj=3.61e-08].

MMP3 has one of the largest pooled increases (log2FC [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.90], padj [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=7.05e-19]) and a smaller but significant protein increase [gene=MMP3; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.806].

CD274 (PD-L1) rises in every cohort (pooled log2FC [gene=CD274; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.97], padj [gene=CD274; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=1.07e-15]), with a small change already in non-inflamed mucosa [gene=CD274; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.197]; the protein was not quantified in the proteomics study.

The CXCR2 increase in inflamed mucosa holds after adjustment for colon segment, age and sex (adjusted log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_adjusted; source=DATASET:GSE193677; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed UC vs control, biopsy level; adjusted_log2fc=2.552], padj [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_adjusted; source=DATASET:GSE193677; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed UC vs control, biopsy level; adjusted_padj=4.53e-28]); being an immune-cell receptor, its bulk change may reflect cell influx.

REG1A replicates only partly: it is not significant in the Leuven infliximab cohort (padj [gene=REG1A; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE16879; layer=rna; cohort=GSE16879; contrast=uc_vs_control; padj=0.132]) nor in the adult colon RNA-seq cohort (padj [gene=REG1A; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE165512; layer=rna; cohort=GSE165512; contrast=uc_vs_control; padj=0.259]), while the paediatric PROTECT cohort shows a very large increase [gene=REG1A; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE109142; layer=rna; cohort=GSE109142; contrast=uc_vs_control; log2fc=8.73].

TNF, the approved target, changes only modestly in the biopsies (pooled log2FC [gene=TNF; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.92], padj [gene=TNF; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=9.06e-08]): the strength of a target is not read from its own mRNA.

OSM rises across the eight cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=OSM; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.46], padj [gene=OSM; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=6.34e-10]) with high heterogeneity (I2 [gene=OSM; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; i2=0.965]).

JAK2, one of the top Open Targets UC targets (score [gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.7318]), shows only a small expression increase in the biopsies [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.874].

CXCR2 transcripts in inflamed UC mucosa come almost entirely from neutrophils (neutrophil share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]), and after composition adjustment its bulk increase falls from [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; unadjusted_log2fc=2.60] to [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.44] (retained fraction [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.17]): mostly neutrophil influx.

In the neutrophil-free Smillie atlas CXCR2 is attributed to T/NK cells (lineage share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.564]) but the second dataset attributes it to myeloid cells, so that attribution does not replicate; the neutrophil dataset is the informative one for this gene.

In situ, neutrophils explain CXCR2 in deconvolved Visium spots (contribution [gene=CXCR2; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.386]) and carry most of its transcripts in Xenium non-inflamed sections [gene=CXCR2; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:GSE312420; attribution_by_state.noninflamed.neutrophil=0.818], confirming the single-cell attribution.
CXCR1 is a neutrophil gene in inflamed UC mucosa (neutrophil share [gene=CXCR1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.962]); its bulk increase marks neutrophil influx.
CXCL8 transcripts in inflamed mucosa come mainly from neutrophils (neutrophil share [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]).

AQP9 is a neutrophil gene (neutrophil share [gene=AQP9; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.92]) and its bulk increase shrinks after composition adjustment to [gene=AQP9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.855] (retained fraction [gene=AQP9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.261]): a marker of neutrophil influx rather than a tissue change.

S100A8 is made mainly by neutrophils in inflamed mucosa (neutrophil share [gene=S100A8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.909]), consistent with faecal calprotectin being a neutrophil marker.
TREM1 transcripts come mostly from neutrophils (neutrophil share [gene=TREM1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.894]).

CHI3L1 is made by inflammatory fibroblasts in the Smillie atlas (share [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.652], expressed in [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.pct_expressing=80.4%] of those cells), replicated at lineage level in the second dataset, with a neutrophil contribution in the neutrophil dataset [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.466].

After composition adjustment CHI3L1 keeps a significant increase, part tissue change and part influx: adjusted log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.40], padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=1.56e-16], retained fraction [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.366].

In deconvolved Visium spots plasma cells explain the largest raw share of CHI3L1 (contribution [gene=CHI3L1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.258]) but the composition-corrected source is inflammatory fibroblasts, which are also enriched around its high spots (log2 enrichment [gene=CHI3L1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; enriched_neighbors.0.log2_enrichment=0.659]); on CosMx it is at background.

MMP1 is an inflammatory-fibroblast gene (share [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.531], stromal attribution replicated) with little neutrophil contribution [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.075]; its increase survives composition adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.26], retained fraction [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.438]).

In situ, inflammatory fibroblasts explain most of MMP1 in deconvolved Visium spots (contribution [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.579]), and its high spots are surrounded by inflammatory fibroblasts and neutrophils (neutrophil log2 enrichment [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; enriched_neighbors.1.log2_enrichment=1.063]): tissue and single cells agree.

IDO1 is attributed to myeloid cells in the Smillie atlas (lineage share [gene=IDO1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.598], replicated), but in the neutrophil dataset enterocytes make most of it [gene=IDO1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed_with_neutrophils.0.share=0.427], and Xenium inflamed sections place it in epithelium [gene=IDO1; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:GSE312420; attribution_by_state.inflamed.epithelial=0.371]: an interferon-induced gene of both epithelium and myeloid cells.

IDO1 keeps a significant change after composition adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.85], padj [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=2.63e-09]); in deconvolved Visium spots epithelium explains most of it [gene=IDO1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.349] while the composition-corrected source is myeloid.

DUOX2 is an epithelial gene (epithelial lineage share [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947], replicated; neutrophil share [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.039]) whose increase survives composition adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.32], padj [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=1.77e-09]).

In inflamed mucosa most CD274 transcripts come from neutrophils (neutrophil share [gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.687]), while in the neutrophil-free atlas myeloid cells dominate [gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.347]; the bulk increase is partly composition (retained fraction [gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.384]).

SERPINB5 is one of the few leading genes whose increase is intrinsic to the tissue: adjusted log2FC [gene=SERPINB5; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=2.109] (padj [gene=SERPINB5; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=2.76e-21]), retained fraction [gene=SERPINB5; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.683], with negligible neutrophil contribution [gene=SERPINB5; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.05].

The HMGCS2 loss shrinks after composition adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=-0.855], retained fraction [gene=HMGCS2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.398]): epithelial lineage scores fall in inflamed mucosa, so the adjustment can over-correct a genuine epithelial loss.

INHBA is attributed to stroma in the Smillie atlas (lineage share [gene=INHBA; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.503]) but to myeloid cells in the second dataset (not replicated); monocyte-derived macrophages make the largest share in the neutrophil dataset [gene=INHBA; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed_with_neutrophils.0.share=0.343], and the bulk change is partly composition (retained fraction [gene=INHBA; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.306]).

CDH3 (P-cadherin) keeps a significant but smaller increase after composition adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=CDH3; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.852], retained fraction [gene=CDH3; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.307]).

TNFa pathway activity is raised in inflamed or UC mucosa in all eight cohorts, strongly in the discovery cohort (t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=17.49], padj [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.padj=2.63e-48]) and in UNIFI (t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=20.07]).

NFkB pathway activity is raised in all eight cohorts (discovery cohort t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=17.48]), and the NFKB1 regulon is among the most active transcription factors (discovery cohort t [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=19.75]).

JAK-STAT pathway activity rises in all eight cohorts (discovery cohort t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=15.68]) and the STAT3 regulon is strongly active (discovery cohort t [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=20.6]): an axis already targeted by JAK inhibitors.

TGFb pathway activity is raised in all eight cohorts, most strongly in UNIFI (t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=25.17]), and EGFR and hypoxia activity also rise consistently (EGFR discovery cohort t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=18.08]).

Not every pathway moves consistently: p53 activity is unchanged in the discovery cohort (padj [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.padj=0.379]) and lower only in some cohorts (Leuven infliximab t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE16879.t=-3.59]), and androgen activity goes in opposite directions across cohorts.

The stress and inflammatory transcription factor AP1 is active in all eight cohorts (discovery cohort t [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=18.4]), while the intestinal identity factor CDX2 loses activity in all eight, most strongly in the paediatric PROTECT rectum (t [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE109142.t=-20.57]).

The strongest CXCL8 circuit is neutrophil-to-endothelium: CXCR4-high neutrophils to ACKR1 venular endothelium (score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_inflamed=7870.993], log2 change vs uninflamed [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=1.324]), with neutrophil-to-neutrophil CXCL8 to CXCR2 pairing towards PADI4 neutrophils (score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_inflamed=3646.664]); co-expression, not proof of signalling.

Inflammatory fibroblasts are the sender of CXCL1 to CXCR2 on neutrophils, a pairing almost absent in uninflamed mucosa (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=3.871], score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_inflamed=443.206]): a stromal neutrophil-recruitment signal that no approved UC drug targets.

The OSM neutrophil-to-fibroblast pairing (OSM-high neutrophils to lamina propria fibroblasts via IL6ST) is not stronger in inflamed than in uninflamed mucosa (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=-0.709], score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_inflamed=139.844]).

IL1B from monocyte-derived macrophages pairs mostly with the decoy receptor IL1R2 on neutrophils (score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_inflamed=4251.623], log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=1.168]), a pairing that would buffer rather than transmit the signal.

TNF from monocyte-derived macrophages pairs with TNFRSF1B on CXCR4-high neutrophils (score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_inflamed=80.329], log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=0.955]): the already-targeted TNF axis links macrophages to neutrophils.

INHBA (activin A) from inflammatory fibroblasts pairs with TGFBR3 on smooth muscle cells only in inflamed mucosa (score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_inflamed=66.463], absent in uninflamed mucosa): an untargeted stromal circuit.

Baseline TNFa pathway activity is higher in non-responders to ustekinumab (t [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.t_nr_vs_r=4.79], padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=4.84e-05]) and infliximab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.000294]) but also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]): it marks severity rather than a drug-specific mechanism.

TGFb pathway activity is associated with non-response to ustekinumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000493]) and infliximab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.0136]), and again in UNIFI placebo (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00984]) and in corticosteroid-treated children (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.corticosteroids (PROTECT).padj=0.0018]).

JAK-STAT activity is associated with non-response to ustekinumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]) but not to vedolizumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.571]) and is borderline in UNIFI placebo (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0543]).

Baseline OSM is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (difference [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.diff_nr_minus_r=0.651], padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=2.64e-05]) but not significantly in UNIFI placebo (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]); the drug-by-expression interaction is null (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.982]), so a drug-specific effect is not shown.

TREM1 is associated with ustekinumab non-response (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=4.74e-05]) and also with UNIFI placebo non-response (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]): a severity marker.

CXCR2 is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders (difference [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.diff_nr_minus_r=0.967], padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-06]) and in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126]): neutrophil burden marks severity.

CHI3L1 is associated with ustekinumab non-response (padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.00971]) and with UNIFI placebo non-response (difference [gene=CHI3L1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).diff_nr_minus_r=1.575], padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0203]), so it marks severity; its correlation with faecal calprotectin in PROTECT is weak (rho [gene=CHI3L1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; faecal_calprotectin_rho_protect=0.198]).

Baseline expression of ITGB7, the vedolizumab target, does not differ between vedolizumab responders and non-responders (difference [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.diff_nr_minus_r=-0.011], padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]): target mRNA does not select patients.
IL23A baseline expression does not separate ustekinumab responders from non-responders (padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]).

TNF expression is not associated with infliximab response (padj [gene=TNF; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.493]) and only weakly with ustekinumab non-response (difference [gene=TNF; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.diff_nr_minus_r=0.218], padj [gene=TNF; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.00969]).

In the adalimumab single-cell atlas CXCL8 does not differ at baseline between remitters and non-remitters; after treatment it falls in cycling mononuclear phagocytes (coef [gene=CXCL8; type=antitnf_singlecell; source=DATASET:GSE282122; after_vs_before_treatment.1.coef=-1.377], padj [gene=CXCL8; type=antitnf_singlecell; source=DATASET:GSE282122; after_vs_before_treatment.1.padj=0.0253]).

After adalimumab, IL1B falls in IL1B-high C1Q-high macrophages (coef [gene=IL1B; type=antitnf_singlecell; source=DATASET:GSE282122; after_vs_before_treatment.0.coef=-1.593], padj [gene=IL1B; type=antitnf_singlecell; source=DATASET:GSE282122; after_vs_before_treatment.0.padj=0.00389]).

After adalimumab CHI3L1 rises in several fibroblast states, for example SOX6-positive POSTN-positive fibroblasts (coef [gene=CHI3L1; type=antitnf_singlecell; source=DATASET:GSE282122; after_vs_before_treatment.0.coef=2.052], padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=antitnf_singlecell; source=DATASET:GSE282122; after_vs_before_treatment.0.padj=5.11e-07]), with no baseline difference between remitters and non-remitters in this small cohort.

CHRDL2 is the leading first-in-class candidate of the discovery screen: up in UC (pooled log2FC [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=2.36]), made by inflammatory fibroblasts (share [gene=CHRDL2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.39], stromal attribution replicated), antibody-tractable and without a clinical drug; but only part of its change survives composition adjustment (retained [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.28]) and it has the highest vital-organ RNA of the shortlist [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6].

CPXM1, a stromal candidate (pooled log2FC [gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=1.89]), retains the largest share of its change among the stromal candidates after composition adjustment [gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.41], is expressed in [gene=CPXM1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.pct_expressing=46.1%] of inflammatory fibroblasts and has low vital-organ RNA [gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=9.1].

XKR9 is the only shortlisted candidate with an intrinsic, composition-resistant change (retained [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.80], epithelial), but it is up in only half of the cohorts, which weakens its replication.

LAX1, a T/NK-cell adaptor up in all cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=1.82]), passes the safety filter (vital-organ RNA [gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=2.5]) but most of its change is lymphocyte influx (retained [gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.23]).

SERPINB5 passes the composition and safety filters (vital-organ RNA [gene=SERPINB5; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=0.3]) but is excluded from the first-in-class list because it is already well studied in UC.

IL12B, the target of ustekinumab, is the top Open Targets UC target (score [gene=IL12B; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.7424]) and has the strongest plasma MR result: higher IL12B protein raises UC risk (OR per SD [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539], q [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; q=1.11e-21]), colocalising with the IBD signal and replicating in FinnGen (OR [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; finngen_odds_ratio_per_sd=1.263]): a positive control.

Genetically higher plasma IL10 lowers UC risk (OR per SD [gene=IL10; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.071], q [gene=IL10; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; q=6.85e-21]), and IL10 knockout mice develop spontaneous colitis (MGI: loss gives or worsens colitis).

Genetically higher plasma PD-L1 (CD274) lowers UC risk (OR per SD [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595], q [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; q=8.57e-08]), colocalising with the IBD signal (posterior [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; colocalisation_h4=0.985]) and replicating in FinnGen (OR [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; finngen_odds_ratio_per_sd=0.734]): its rise in the mucosa is likely protective, so blocking it with the checkpoint drugs listed in Open Targets is the wrong direction; agonism would be the hypothesis.

CD274 is not strongly constrained (LOEUF [gene=CD274; type=target_safety; source=DATASET:SAFETY; loeuf=0.476]) and has no curated safety events; its MR shows instrument heterogeneity (p [gene=CD274; type=mr_sensitivity; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; layer=plasma_protein; heterogeneity_p=0.0259]) but a concordant weighted median [gene=CD274; type=mr_sensitivity; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; layer=plasma_protein; weighted_median=-0.487] and the correct Steiger direction.

CXCR2 has the highest convergence score, with Open Targets genetic association [gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8171] and clinical small molecules (reparixin, phase 3 in another indication) but no UC drug; it has no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument, so MR could not test it, and it is unconstrained (LOEUF [gene=CXCR2; type=target_safety; source=DATASET:SAFETY; loeuf=1.154]).

CXCR2 has been perturbed in mouse colitis in many papers [gene=CXCR2; type=mouse_colitis_literature; source=DATASET:EUROPEPMC_MOUSE; mouse_colitis_papers=19], including a selective antagonist that ameliorated acute experimental colitis, but MGI records no colitis phenotype for a single-gene model.

CHI3L1 has no genetic support: the plasma MR is null (OR per SD [gene=CHI3L1; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.903], q [gene=CHI3L1; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; q=0.577]) and does not replicate in FinnGen, and the colon eQTL MR is also null (q [gene=CHI3L1; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=colon_tissue; q=0.275]); it is antibody and small-molecule tractable with no clinical drug.

Despite its large expression change, CXCL8 has a weak Open Targets association with UC (score [gene=CXCL8; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.1087]) and no genetic association.

FCGR2A has strong Open Targets genetic association [gene=FCGR2A; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.87] but the UK Biobank plasma MR is null (q [gene=FCGR2A; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; q=0.916]); FinnGen gives a protective estimate (OR [gene=FCGR2A; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; finngen_odds_ratio_per_sd=0.86]) and the combined estimate is only marginal (q [gene=FCGR2A; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; combined_q=0.0366]).
TREM1 is tractable by small molecules and antibodies and has a clinical-stage inhibitor (nangibotide, phase 2), but its expression comes from neutrophils and associates with severity.
ITGB7 is an approved UC target (vedolizumab, phase 4; etrolizumab, phase 3) and serves as a positive control for druggability.
TNF is among the top Open Targets UC targets (score [gene=TNF; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.6336]), the positive control for an approved mechanism.

In colon tissue eQTL MR, higher GSDMA expression raises UC risk (OR per SD [gene=GSDMA; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=colon_tissue; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.131], q [gene=GSDMA; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=colon_tissue; q=4.49e-12]) but does not colocalise with the IBD signal, so a neighbouring causal variant cannot be excluded.

Higher IRF8 expression in transverse colon raises UC risk (OR per SD [gene=IRF8; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=colon_tissue; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.937], q [gene=IRF8; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=colon_tissue; q=2.36e-07]) and colocalises with the IBD signal: a gut-specific genetic lead.

The literature reports CHI3L1 upregulated in UC and correlated with NLRP3 inflammasome expression, and that it promotes macrophage pyroptosis through BCAT1-mediated NF-kappaB activation; inhibition was protective in that single study.

The literature places the CXCL8 to CXCR1 and CXCR2 axis in UC pathogenesis through PI3K/Akt, MAPK and NF-kappaB signalling, and reports CXCL8 as a blood diagnostic marker of IBD; the evidence is reviews and bioinformatic signatures rather than trials.
A single study reports IDO1 elevated in UC, driving M1 macrophage polarisation via the GRP78-XBP1 ER-stress pathway, and that an IDO1 inhibitor ameliorated DSS colitis in mice.
The literature links calprotectin transcripts (S100A8) to endoscopic disease activity and names S100A8 a credible diagnostic biomarker of UC.
DUOX2 is reported upregulated in IBD together with MMP10, LCN2 and REG genes, and one study of a herbal formula proposes it as a therapeutic target; literature support as a drug target is thin.
The literature reports HMGCS2 decreased in UC with high diagnostic value, consistent with the expression loss.
MMP1 is reported among transcripts modified by mirikizumab that correlate with disease activity indices, and as a diagnostic biomarker in a bioinformatic study.

A single study reports AQP9 expressed mainly in neutrophils, promoting NET formation via JAK2-STAT3-mediated pyroptosis and aggravating epithelial injury in UC, which agrees with its neutrophil attribution here.
SERPINB5 is reported increased in UC and in TNF-treated epithelial cells, and to bind and stabilise MMP9, sustaining its activity.

CXCR2 has no verbatim-validated literature relation in this corpus; PubTator machine extraction finds [gene=CXCR2; type=pubtator_relations; source=DATASET:PUBTATOR3_RELATIONS; relations=25] relations in [gene=CXCR2; type=pubtator_relations; source=DATASET:PUBTATOR3_RELATIONS; publications=11] publications, all plain associations with UC, so its literature support is weaker than its ranking suggests.
CXCL1 is reported overexpressed in pancolitis and as one of the genes of a diagnostic model of UC.

caveats: Single-agent run: the same tools as the six specialists, with fewer calls per stream.
Composition adjustment can over-correct when resident cells become activated; loss of significance is not proof of influx.
Treatment associations are baseline associations, not predictions; placebo arms identify severity markers.
Co-expression of ligand and receptor is not proof of signalling.
